config.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG

intro.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates the concepts of server-side rendering (SSR) and static site generation (SSG) to understand how they differ from client-side rendering. You'll learn how to pre-render content on the server for faster initial page loads and better SEO, similar to React's SSR and SSG approaches. The core programming concept involves configuring Vue's build tools to generate static HTML or use a Node.js server for on-demand rendering. You'll work with Vue components, build configurations, and basic server concepts, all within a beginner-friendly Vue context.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building high-performance, content-heavy applications like e-commerce product pages, news websites, and social media feeds. For example, an e-commerce site uses Server-Side Rendering (SSR) to ensure product listings and details are immediately visible for SEO and fast initial load, while interactive elements like shopping cart buttons are handled client-side. Static Site Generation (SSG) is perfect for marketing pages, blogs, or documentation where content changes infrequently, enabling lightning-fast delivery from a CDN. Understanding when to use each approach allows developers to optimize performance and user experience in real-world projects like dashboards that blend static data panels with dynamic, user-specific widgets.

objectives: Implement a Vue component that fetches and renders data on the server using server-side rendering (SSR)
Configure a Vue application to generate static HTML pages at build time using static site generation (SSG)
Construct a Vue component that conditionally renders content based on whether it's executing on the server or client
Integrate server-side data fetching with client-side interactivity in a Vue component
Manipulate Vue's rendering modes to optimize performance for different types of content
Initialize a Vue project with both SSR and SSG capabilities using appropriate build configurations
Apply hydration techniques to attach Vue's reactivity to server-rendered HTML

steps.hint: Use async/await with setTimeout to simulate server latency. Return a simple object like { message: 'Data from server' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: An async fetchServerData function is defined inside setup, ready to be called to simulate server-side data fetching.
successCriteria: The fetchServerData function is defined with async keyword, uses Promise with setTimeout, and returns mock data object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is async, uses setTimeout to create delay, and returns a Promise with mock data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create an async function named fetchServerData that returns a Promise resolving after a delay.

steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property named 'formattedTime' is created in the setup function, returning a formatted time string.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property wasn't created correctly. Remember to use Vue's computed function and return a formatted time string from within the setup function.
